title: How to compare expense management software as a UAE real estate company
summary: Choosing expense management software for a UAE property business? Learn what to check across entities, property coding, cards, VAT, receipts, and accounting.
body_markdown:
By the time a property finance team gets a receipt, the useful context has often disappeared with it. Say someone on site bought the materials three weeks ago. The card statement shows the supplier, but not the property or project. The receipt is buried in WhatsApp. And now your finance team has to chase the person who made the purchase just to work out where the cost belongs.


That might be manageable for a handful of transactions. But across multiple properties, entities, and site teams, it becomes a control problem. This is where[spend management software](https://www.alaan.com/industries/real-estate) for real estate groups needs to do more than digitise receipts. It needs to capture, control, and route spend correctly from the moment someone makes a purchase.


## Why property businesses need a different approach to expense management


Property businesses have a few layers of complexity that a standard expense workflow does not always account for. This includes things like:


- Multiple entities: Property groups often manage several entities across developments, properties, or business operations. Spend needs to be tracked against the right entity from the start.
- Property and project-level spend: A generic category like “maintenance” is not enough. Finance needs to know which property, project, or cost centre the expense belongs to.
- Teams spend away from finance: Site managers, engineers, and facilities teams often buy what they need while moving between properties. They need spending flexibility without losing financial control.
- Your accounting system stays in place: Expense management needs to work with the property accounting platform you already use, feeding it clean data and supporting accounting automation instead of adding another manual process.


That is why the[best expense management software](https://www.alaan.com/blog/best-expense-tracking-software-small-business) for a property business is not necessarily the one with the longest feature list. If you are evaluating expense management software in the UAE, start with these four realities. They determine what you should expect from every vendor you consider.


## Six questions to ask before choosing expense management software


A good demo can make almost any expense tool look impressive. The better test is whether it can handle the messy parts of your actual spend: multiple entities, properties, site teams, accounting workflows, and UAE tax requirements.


Ask every vendor these six questions, and pay attention to how they answer rather than how many features appear on the screen.


### 1. Can you manage spend across multiple entities?


Can we set up our different legal entities separately, with the right users, cards, approvals, budgets, and reporting for each?


If your group has several entities, you need more than a company-wide expense dashboard. A good answer should explain how the system keeps entities separate while still giving your finance team the visibility to manage group-wide spend.


Look for clear controls around who can spend for each entity, how transactions are assigned, and how reporting works across the group.


### 2. Can employees code spend to the right property or project when they buy?


Can we require the property, project, or cost centre to be selected at the point of spend?


This matters because fixing coding after the transaction is already sitting in finance is slow and error-prone. If a site manager buys materials for Building A, you should not have to chase them three weeks later to find out where the expense belongs.


A good answer should show how property or project information is captured as part of the spending workflow, with rules or required fields where appropriate.


### 3. Can the data flow into our property accounting platform?


How does the system export or sync expense data with the accounting platform we already use?


You are adding an[expense management](https://www.alaan.com/products/expense-management) layer, not replacing your property accounting system. The right solution should reduce manual reconciliation rather than give finance another system to maintain.


Ask the vendor to show you the actual data flow: what information is exported, in what format, how often, and what happens when something does not match.


### 4. Can site staff use cards without giving up control?


Can we issue cards to site teams with spending limits and controls that reflect what they actually need to buy?


Your site teams may need to make urgent purchases without waiting for finance to approve every small transaction. That does not mean giving everyone an unrestricted[corporate card](https://www.alaan.com/products/corporate-cards) .


When comparing corporate credit card expense management software, look for controls around limits, categories, merchants, users, and approvals. Also ask what happens when someone needs to make an exception.


### 5. Can receipts be captured when people are in the field?


What happens when someone makes a purchase on site and has poor connectivity or cannot immediately access the finance system?


A receipt workflow that works perfectly in an office is not necessarily useful for a property business. Your teams may be moving between buildings, construction sites, or facilities where connectivity is unreliable.


A good answer should explain how receipts are captured, matched to transactions, and submitted when the employee is back online. Test this yourself rather than accepting a demo at face value.


### 6. Does it support UAE VAT requirements?


How does the system help us capture the information we need to assess input VAT recovery?


The software should not be expected to replace your tax team's judgement. But it should make it easier to retain the transaction and invoice information they need.


Ask how the system handles tax information, tax invoices, and supporting documentation, and whether that information remains attached to the transaction when data moves into your accounting workflow. This is particularly important when evaluating expense management software in the UAE, where poor documentation can create problems long after the original purchase.


## Not every impressive feature needs to make the shortlist


A polished demo can make almost any feature look essential. But for a property finance team, some things are nice to have rather than reasons to choose one vendor over another.


You probably do not need to spend hours comparing:


- Fancy dashboards: Useful for visibility, but they will not fix poorly coded transactions.
- Dozens of report templates: More options do not necessarily mean better reporting. What matters is whether you can get the property, entity, project, and spend data you actually need.
- Custom branding: Nice if you care about the experience, but it has little bearing on financial control.
- Gamified employee experiences: Encouraging people to submit expenses on time can help, but it is not a substitute for a workflow that captures the right information upfront.
- An endless list of integrations: A vendor can have 100 integrations and still not connect cleanly to the property accounting platform you use.


The point is not to ignore these features. It is to test them after the fundamentals. If a vendor cannot handle your entities, property coding, site spend, accounting workflow, or VAT requirements, a beautiful dashboard will not save the implementation.


## Put the software through your actual month-end


A demo shows you what a platform can do. A real trial shows you what your finance team will actually have to deal with.


Run one month of real, representative spend through your shortlisted tools. Include the awkward stuff: purchases from site teams, different entities, missing receipts, property-level coding, approvals, and transactions that need VAT information. Bring one site team into the trial, too. If the workflow slows them down, you will know before rolling it out across the business.


For example, if you are considering[Alaan](https://www.alaan.com/) , use the trial to test how its corporate cards, spend controls, receipt capture, VAT data, and accounting workflows handle your actual transactions. Do not just test the happy path. Put a real site purchase through the system, allocate it to the right property, attach the invoice, run it through approval, and see what reaches your accounting workflow.


At the end, measure five things:


1. How many transactions needed manual correction?
2. How often did finance have to chase receipts or coding details?
3. How much spend was correctly assigned to the right entity and property?
4. How clean was the data when it reached your accounting system?
5. How much time did the finance team spend preparing for month-end?


The right tool should make those numbers better. That is more useful than any feature demo.


## What do expense management software cost


Expense management software can cost anywhere from a few dollars per user each month to several hundred dirhams for a broader business plan. Capterra puts entry-level expense-report software at roughly[14 to 45 dollars per month](https://www.capterra.com/expense-report-software/) , but pricing varies widely by users, features, and billing model.


For a property business, look beyond the subscription price. Ask whether you will pay extra for implementation, additional cards, accounting integrations, premium support, or foreign-currency transactions. FX fees can matter more than the software fee if your teams regularly pay overseas suppliers.


Alaan, for example, has a[free Starter plan](https://www.alaan.com/pricing) for up to 10 users and a Premium plan at AED 499 per month, with Enterprise pricing available for larger or more customised requirements. The Premium plan includes unlimited users, ERP integrations, automated expense features, and AI capabilities.


## Final thoughts


The right expense management software should fit the way your property business already operates: across entities, properties, projects, and site teams.


Start with those realities, test shortlisted platforms using your own transactions, and look beyond the demo to the work your finance team still has to do afterwards. ## FAQs


1. What does expense management software do?


It helps businesses control, track, approve, and record employee spending, while capturing receipts and sending accurate expense data to accounting systems.


2. How do you choose expense management software for a property business?


Look for multi-entity support, property-level coding, accounting integrations, controlled cards, field receipt capture, and UAE VAT capabilities.


3. How much does expense management software cost?


Pricing varies by users, features, and billing model. Check the subscription alongside implementation, card, integration, and foreign-currency transaction costs.


4. Does expense management software replace property accounting software?


Usually, no. It sits alongside your accounting platform, capturing and controlling spend before sending structured, coded data into your existing finance system.
